subject: DPA negotiation: data retention + backup/DR carve-outs for NovusHealth PoC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Hayes <lucy.hayes@novushealth.com>, procurement@novushealth.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA negotiation: data retention + backup/DR carve-outs for NovusHealth PoC

Hi Lucy / team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday — excited about the PoC next month. Legal on both sides asked me to kick off a short thread to align on a couple of DPA items before we sign, specifically retention, deletion, and a limited backup/DR carve-out we discussed.

Two quick calls-outs from our side:
- Retention: Novus requested 12 months for certain logs. We typically default to 90 days for production data but can support longer for logs/metrics with a narrow scope.
- Backup/DR carve-out: we need a small exception so that backups made for Disaster Recovery are retained per our DR schedule (90 days) and can be restored only for operational continuity; those backups will be inaccessible for product feature use.

I attached an initial redline (Novus_DPA_redline_v1.pdf) with inline comments where we think carve-out language should go. Can you review and let us know if the DR carve-out as framed is acceptable, and whether Novus needs a specific audit or logging commitment tied to restores?

If it helps, Marissa (cc’d) can propose alternative language we can sign via DocuSign.

Best,
Jordan
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

Attachment: Novus_DPA_redline_v1.pdf (pdf, 42KB)

From: Lucy Hayes <lucy.hayes@novushealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novushealth.com, Victor Chen <contracts@novushealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-30T12:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA negotiation: data retention + backup/DR carve-outs for NovusHealth PoC

Jordan — thanks for the note and the redline. Couple of quick clarifications from our side before we loop Legal formally:

1) Retention: For the PoC we can accept 90 days for customer data, but need 12 months for audit logs and system telemetry that will be used for compliance reporting.
2) Backup/DR carve-out: We are uncomfortable with a carve-out that allows restored backups to exist beyond customer access controls. Any restoration event should be logged and be subject to the same deletion/retention policies.
3) Subprocessors: please provide the latest subprocessor list and confirm whether any three-letter subcontractors are used for backups (e.g., storage providers, cross-region replication).

Victor from Contracts is looped in — he’ll take the legal review.

Thanks,
Lucy Hayes
Head of Platform Ops, NovusHealth
lucy.hayes@novushealth.com

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Novus’ quick reply. They want 12 months for audit logs and tighter controls around restores. They also asked for the full subprocessor list and whether any storage replication partners are used.

Can Legal propose final language that:
- Allows a narrowly scoped DR backup retention (90 days) specifically for operational recovery,
- Ensures any restore events are logged and subject to the same access controls and deletion on request,
- Confirms subprocessor transparency and a standard notification period for changes.

If we can land language that is acceptable to both, I’ll send the DocuSign to Victor/Lucy.

Thanks —
Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Hayes <lucy.hayes@novushealth.com>, Victor Chen <contracts@novushealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-01T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA negotiation: data retention + backup/DR carve-outs for NovusHealth PoC

Hi Lucy / Victor — appreciate the quick turnaround. I’ve reviewed Novus’ asks and propose the attached counter-redline (Redwood_DPA_response_v2.pdf). High-level summary of our position: 

1) Retention
- Customer content: Redwood will retain customer-provided content for 90 days post-termination/contract end for the PoC. We can make an exception for audit logs/telemetry up to 12 months, but only if Novus confirms a documented, business-justified need and accepts a scoped access/usage clause limited to compliance reporting.

2) Backup / DR carve-out
- Proposed carve-out language allows Redwood to retain disaster recovery backups for up to 90 days solely for operational recovery.
- Any restore of a backup for a customer must be: (a) initiated only for remediation/operational continuity, (b) logged in our restore audit trail, and (c) limited to the data necessary to recover the service. Restores will be subject to Novus’ access controls in effect at time of restore and logged in the audit trail; we will provide restore logs on request for compliance review.

3) Subprocessors and transfers
- We attached the current subprocessor list as an appendix (s3-like storage provider in us-west-2 for backups). We will provide 30 days’ notice for material changes and will remain the controller/processor point of contact.
- Cross-border transfers: we can rely on SCCs for EU->US data; we will provide a standard transfer addendum if needed.

4) Execution
- We prefer DocuSign for a faster turnaround and have prepared a pre-filled envelope. If Novus requires AdobeSign, we can accommodate — just let us know which signing URL to use.

I’ve attached the redlined DPA and the subprocessor appendix. If Victor is comfortable with the compromise on logs/restore logging, please counter-sign. Happy to hop on a short call if any nuance needs a quick sync.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_response_v2.pdf (pdf, 55KB), Subprocessor_Appendix.csv (csv, 4KB)

Subject: Re: DPA negotiation: data retention + backup/DR carve-outs for NovusHealth PoC

Marissa — thanks for the detailed response and the appendix. A few items from Contracts: 

1) Audit logs: Novus requires 12 months for audit logs as a non-negotiable compliance requirement for the PoC. We acknowledge your ask for a documented business justification — we will provide a short statement from our compliance team.
2) Restore access controls: Novus will accept restores limited to operational recovery if Redwood supplies a restore audit within 48 hours of any event and confirms that restored data will not be used for feature development or analytics.
3) Subprocessor notice: 30 days’ notice is acceptable. Please confirm whether any subcontractor has access to decrypted customer content during normal operations.
4) Execution: Novus prefers AdobeSign for all procurement docs due to internal workflow; please send the AdobeSign initiation link.

If you can incorporate the 12-month audit log requirement into section 4.2 with the access-limits we discussed, Novus Legal is ready to sign once AdobeSign is staged.

Regards,
Victor Chen
Contracts Manager, NovusHealth
contracts@novushealth.com

2) Marissa will also add the restore-audit commitment (Redwood provides restore logs within 48 hours and confirms no feature/analytics use).
3) Marissa will prepare the final DPA and upload to AdobeSign per Novus preference — Victor, please confirm the recipient email to use for the envelope staging.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.
